name: MasTec
employees: ~36,000 (Dec 2025, 10-K) — ~39,000 with the Jul 2026 Superior Group close

ownership.notes: Mas family-led: CEO Jose R. Mas, Chairman Jorge Mas. Key operating brands: Wanzek Construction (wind, since 2008), IEA Constructors/White Construction (acquired Oct 2022, ~$1.1B), Henkels & McCoy (Power Delivery, 2021), T&D Power (Greenlink), MasTec Professional Services, The Superior Group (data-center electrical, ~$1.65B, closed Jul 2026).

summary: BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT: MasTec is the diversified giant of the batch — ENR's #6 contractor ($14.3B FY2025 revenue, record $21.4B backlog at Q2 2026) spanning renewables construction (Clean Energy & Infrastructure: $4.7B revenue, $7.8B backlog, arguably the #1 US wind constructor via Wanzek + IEA with ~21 GW+ built), grid (Power Delivery: $5.6B+ backlog including its second-largest transmission award ever and NV Energy's $4.2B Greenlink West), fiber (Communications), and now a full AIDC pivot: ~$1B of Q4 2025 data-center bookings including its first turnkey data-center construction-management award, the $1.65B Superior Group acquisition for inside-the-fence electrical, hyperscaler pursuits each >$1B, and RICE/simple-cycle gas plants for bridge power. Its only documented BESS OEM pairing is Sungrow — twice in 2025 (Vitis Energy's Apache Hill 200 MW/400 MWh, MasTec EPC; and Onyx Renewables' distributed portfolio) — proving no blanket China aversion at the EPC level, though equipment remains predominantly owner-furnished. Investor Day targets ~$22B revenue and >$15 adjusted EPS by 2028 on grid + data-center demand.
ecosystemRole: We assess MasTec as the most AIDC-committed EPC in the batch and a bellwether for how construction capacity is rotating toward data centers: telecom fiber + T&D + generation + storage + now inside-the-fence electrical under one roof, with management explicitly chasing hyperscaler projects >$1B each. In the BESS web it plays the standard EPC role — constructability gatekeeper on owner-furnished equipment, with alliance relationships (Apex, ACCIONA, Enel, NextEra-class developers, Vitis, Onyx) holding the procurement pen — but with two genuine procurement doors: MasTec Professional Services' full-EPC BESS packages (a documented 65 MW/260 MWh Georgia design-procure-install) and turnkey CE&I scopes where owners delegate BOS/BESS procurement. The Sungrow precedent (Apache Hill, Onyx) is the field's clearest evidence that a Chinese-headquartered supplier can ride owner selection through a top-tier US EPC — the constraint is the owner's tax-credit math, not the contractor.

productsAndServices.name: Clean Energy & Infrastructure (renewables + industrial + gas gen)
productsAndServices.description: FY2025 segment revenue $4.70B (7.4% adj. EBITDA margin), Q2 2026 $1.62B (+43%); 18-month backlog $7.8B (Jun 2026) after a 2.1x book-to-bill Q4 2025; renewables sub-backlog >$3B with ~$4B more 'under contract or limited NTP' outside reported backlog. Mix ~60-65% solar, 35-40% wind; storage share unquantified but 'a core component across projects.' Heritage: Wanzek (17+ GW wind; ~21 GW total clean energy; energy-storage service line) + IEA (260+ utility-scale projects at acquisition). Named BESS work: Apache Hill Energy Center (Vitis Energy — 200 MW/400 MWh standalone, Hood Co. TX, Sungrow BESS, MasTec Renewables EPC, financial close Jun 2025, COD target Jul 2026); MasTec Professional Services full-EPC 65 MW/260 MWh Georgia BESS; Wanzek's Azure Sky listing (Enel hybrid 350 MW wind + 137 MW/180 MWh). Also pursuing simple-cycle and RICE gas plants for data-center bridge power.
productsAndServices.positioning: Arguably #1 US wind constructor (ENR #1 wind, #2 solar in sourcebook-era ranks); absent from Solar Power World lists only because MasTec brands don't report to them — volume understated in specialist rankings.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Long-term alliance agreements with top-tier developers (the stated CE&I moat); three of the four largest wind projects in company history were in backlog as of Q3 2025.
productsAndServices.targetSegments: Utility-scale developers and utilities; industrial; gas generation for large loads.
productsAndServices.roadmap: FY2026 segment guide ~$6.8B — renewables revenue grew >60% in Q1 2026.

productsAndServices.name: AIDC platform (turnkey data centers + inside-the-fence + fiber)
productsAndServices.description: Q4 2025: ~$1B of data-center bookings including the first construction-management agreement for a full turnkey site (customer undisclosed; 2026-27 execution). Superior Group (closed Jul 20, 2026, ~$1.65B): Columbus OH inside-the-fence electrical contractor for data centers/mission-critical — ~3,000 employees, 2026E revenue $1.6-1.7B, ~$1.4B backlog, contributing $800M revenue/$100M EBITDA to H2 2026. Active pursuits: multiple hyperscaler-related projects each >$1B (most revenue 2027+) plus 'billions' in hyperscaler fiber connectivity. Power Delivery serves 'utility clients, data center developers, and hyperscalers' — record $5.6B backlog including the second-largest transmission/substation award in company history; Greenlink West (NV Energy, $4.2B program, 525 kV/~350 mi) built by T&D Power, in-service after summer 2027.
productsAndServices.positioning: One of very few US contractors combining CM + civil + power + telecom + maintenance for data centers (CEO framing); the 2028 Investor Day targets (~$22B revenue, >$15 EPS) are anchored on grid + data-center demand.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Turnkey CM agreements, electrical subcontracts (Superior), utility programs (Greenlink), fiber frameworks.
productsAndServices.targetSegments: Hyperscalers (unnamed), data-center developers, utilities under large-load growth.
productsAndServices.roadmap: Self-perform share of turnkey data-center work to rise on future jobs; 'exponential' DC growth ambition.

productsAndServices.name: Procurement model & equipment interfaces
productsAndServices.description: 10-K boilerplate: under many contracts customers furnish materials (MasTec installs without cost/warranty responsibility); under certain others MasTec purchases on behalf of customers; 'not dependent on any one vendor.' On entering manufacturing: 'We have not looked at getting into manufacturing... really good partners that can support us' (Mas, Q4 2025). Documented BESS pairings: Sungrow twice (Apache Hill via Vitis; Onyx Renewables portfolio — MasTec EPC partner + Sungrow USA supplier). No documented Tesla/Fluence/Powin/LG/Samsung/CATL/Hithium install surfaced — owner announcements, not MasTec's, carry supplier news.
productsAndServices.positioning: Channel and constructability gatekeeper; procurement decision-maker only in Professional Services full-EPC packages and delegated turnkey scopes.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: n/a — describes the contract structures above.
productsAndServices.roadmap: No FEOC statement on record; safe-harbor framing (Q2 2025: 'clear path for safe harboring... construction through 2030') and top-tier-developer skew keep its pipeline credit-eligible — i.e., structurally away from §154-named content.

strategyRead: (High confidence) We assess MasTec as a constructability channel with two genuine procurement doors: most equipment is owner-furnished (10-K contract language, the Sungrow pairings both owner-selected), but MasTec Professional Services' full-EPC BESS packages (65 MW/260 MWh Georgia) and delegated turnkey CE&I scopes are real EPC-procured lanes at mid-scale — the only Batch C firm with a documented design-procure-install BESS credential.

(High confidence) We assess the Sungrow precedent (Apache Hill + Onyx, both 2025) as the field's best evidence that Chinese-headquartered BESS suppliers remain buildable through top-tier US EPCs post-OBBBA — with the caveat that Sungrow's US entity and bankability profile differ from a §154-named cell maker, and both selections were the owner's.

(High confidence) We assess the AIDC pivot as diluting BESS salience at this account: management attention and capital (Superior, turnkey CM, RICE gas, fiber) is rotating to data-center scope where hyperscaler procurement screens on Chinese content are strictest — MasTec will follow its customers' standards, not challenge them.

(Moderate confidence) We assess MasTec's FEOC posture as outsourced to its customers by design: no FEOC statement exists; the stated strategy is safe-harbored, top-tier-developer projects that keep credits — which structurally selects FEOC-compliant equipment onto its sites without MasTec ever taking a position.

(Moderate confidence) For the Hithium lens: the actionable surfaces are (1) MasTec Professional Services and Wanzek's storage BOP practice for EPC-procured mid-scale packages, (2) alliance-developer introductions (Vitis-class owners who already buy Chinese systems), and (3) install-compatibility qualification like Blattner/SOLV. Track the unnamed turnkey data-center customer and the >$1B hyperscaler pursuits as the map of where US construction capacity — and therefore near-term BESS attach — is actually going.

relationships.note: The only documented BESS OEM pairing — twice in 2025 (Apache Hill 200 MW/400 MWh; Onyx distributed portfolio), both owner-selected, MasTec-built.
relationships.context:
Vitis Energy's Apache Hill (200 MW/400 MWh, Hood Co. TX — Sungrow supply, MasTec Renewables EPC, financial close June 2025, COD target July 2026) and Onyx Renewables' $260M distributed solar+storage portfolio (MasTec EPC partner + Sungrow USA supplier, June 2025) are the field's clearest evidence that a Chinese-headquartered BESS supplier rides owner selection through a top-tier US EPC.

The caveat the dossier keeps: equipment is predominantly owner-furnished (10-K contract language; both Sungrow selections were the owner's) — the constraint on Chinese hardware is the owner's tax-credit math, not the contractor.
